key_concept: The SAN is the pacemaker of the heart; it generates the maximum number of action potentials, about $70-75$ per minute, which sets the normal heart rate.
steps: The sino-atrial node (SAN) is a patch of nodal tissue in the right upper corner of the right atrium. The question writes 'sino-arterial', but it means the sino-atrial node.
Nodal tissue is autoexcitable: it can generate action potentials without any external stimulus.
The SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials of any nodal tissue, about $70-75$ per minute.
Because its rate is the highest, the SAN initiates and sets the rhythm of contraction. This is why it is called the pacemaker.
So the normal heart rate is $72$ beats per minute, which falls within the $70-75$ range.
why_not_others: $28-30$ is far too slow for the SAN; much slower inherent rates belong to lower pacemaker tissue, such as the ventricular conducting system, which takes over only when higher pacemakers fail. $100-110$ and $120-140$ correspond to tachycardia (heart rate above $100$ per minute), not the resting rate in a healthy person.
common_trap: Students sometimes confuse the SAN rate with the AVN rate or with exercise heart rates, and pick a higher or lower range.
time_saving_tip: One SAN action potential produces one heartbeat, so the SAN rate equals the normal heart rate of about $72$ per minute. Pick the option containing $72$.
